| Fellow American,

There is a very concerning trend occurring in our country that has me worried for Americans who hold to biblical & faith-based values. [](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=130828190de74a4ba67362c1ad449293&_e=pkstZ9zJu3omw-ijRi6L0VkwFswr5XWBxkox0Dqv74iTSO0R0a1gqIhJDA8YSSMMmG4Z_pqjQU213vOxBbhKmXiI3uRwzPSZ-28_NX2cGk2xhK4iuJcjX_E-ytmeBsaokHX1oYxvhl8EWm90Sat0_sKNqMF1mrxS4gDqlAloaeAiWE2p9TORcNBxNz1O-RqJcyi5fvh92Fen1RDwci6wGYeYdRPBnlfQQ7DBsJ2VBlE2YZ8hxcLXkitiq6NYCrhWPqnRrHXSrsMMq6xXqRjssVoUmyTJie1BkXEvbyPAICWsBz7-TJ4hyCJM_KO9FvMMnYNdhTK3yp8OFPvDafm4GpFSd-2V0VRvxi8thTT81COWzybpDYwIbkmsf_kHHv-4xBKi0upipb97Mxg7HOJNBqt9ldlwoKx7WHTXSf-nHtA%3D) After the _Respect for Marriage Act_ was passed by a bi-partisan effort and signed into law, I am fearful that legal persecution will only intensify against Americans holding to faith-based values and who wish to conduct their lives according to their faith.

[**Are you concerned that America is abandoning a basic tenet of our founding -_Religious Liberty?_**](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=130828190de74a4ba67362c1ad449293&_e=pkstZ9zJu3omw-ijRi6L0VkwFswr5XWBxkox0Dqv74iTSO0R0a1gqIhJDA8YSSMMmG4Z_pqjQU213vOxBbhKmXiI3uRwzPSZ-28_NX2cGk2xhK4iuJcjX_E-ytmeBsaokHX1oYxvhl8EWm90Sat0_sKNqMF1mrxS4gDqlAloaeAiWE2p9TORcNBxNz1O-RqJcyi5fvh92Fen1RDwci6wGYeYdRPBnlfQQ7DBsJ2VBlE2YZ8hxcLXkitiq6NYCrhWqrLVkDr1WuxyiWSrUQ1spkQbRgeNJuD5b1OnXZh69FOIWmWb21JpmVSShcuW8btj0PhRS5G0TqfABOngLynJ8AYJthIBRYbJKpD2pwqS6cG0I__EKdcTJfDPVn6kokcGDHJXeWZJIFH8pk7f9Nvrbmf3PKEB6dNbkH6IlzJuGiQ%3D)

In addition to the passing of the _Respect for Marriage Act_ , numerous examples over the past decade have concerned me: KENNEDY v. BREMERTON SCHOOL DISTRICT, MASTERPIECE CAKESHOP v. COLORADO CIVIL RIGHTS COMMISSION, and 303 CREATIVE v. ELENIS are just a few examples of legal persecution against Americans holding to faith-based values who wish to conduct their lives according to their faith.

Furthermore, an amendment to the _Respect for Marriage Act_ , brought forth by Senator Mike Lee, prohibiting the Federal Government from retaliating against schools, businesses, and organizations because of their religious beliefs about same-sex marriage failed.

**This has the potential to only intensify legal persecution against individuals, businesses, churches, and nonprofits holding to faith-based values. **

The American Cornerstone Institute is a non-profit that I founded to preserve and promote the cornerstones that laid the foundation for the greatest nation the world has ever seen: Faith, Liberty, Community, and Life.

Whether it is a football coach losing his job for praying at midfield after a game, or a baker being sued for not wanting to bake a cake that violates his religious values, **are you concerned as I am with the increase in legal persecution against Americans who wish to conduct their lives according to their faith?**

Please share your thoughts in this quick 2-minute survey concerning religious liberty in America.

**[https://offers.americancornerstone.org/religious-liberty-survey/](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=130828190de74a4ba67362c1ad449293&_e=pkstZ9zJu3omw-ijRi6L0VkwFswr5XWBxkox0Dqv74iTSO0R0a1gqIhJDA8YSSMMmG4Z_pqjQU213vOxBbhKmXiI3uRwzPSZ-28_NX2cGk2xhK4iuJcjX_E-ytmeBsaokHX1oYxvhl8EWm90Sat0_sKNqMF1mrxS4gDqlAloaeAiWE2p9TORcNBxNz1O-RqJcyi5fvh92Fen1RDwci6wGYeYdRPBnlfQQ7DBsJ2VBlE2YZ8hxcLXkitiq6NYCrhWPqnRrHXSrsMMq6xXqRjssZk8K_ojIMMk5G8WA6icBGUBgn8XKi7R0AxLW-gzDdP-KBwWoCJLCB36JGUik1lifryYQlJ26pFtQjG34oc-lDAcXx0NlI5w0J7EdmLfh85cl585AbvADIDOIkimFtChvkfcWp89gFQ3FZ65B-_mU4k%3D)**

Thank you for your consideration.

Regards,

Dr. Ben Carson
Founder & Chairman American Cornerstone Institute

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/virginians-for-jay-jones [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/virginians-for-jay-jones]
Friend,
I hope you will take a moment to read my op-ed with Senator Schuyler VanValkenburg in The Richmond Times-Dispatch in support of commonsense gun safety.
Just last month, legislation regulating “ghost guns,” firearms that are easily assembled and lack serial numbers, was vetoed. Ghost guns can be purchased without a background check, making it easier for these weapons to fall into the hands of bad actors. I was proud to be part of the team that [https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2022/08/11/dc-ghost-guns-polymer80-judgment/] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2022/08/11/dc-ghost-guns-polymer80-judgment/] successfully sued [https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2022/08/11/dc-ghost-guns-polymer80-judgment/] Polymer80, one of the nation’s largest manufacturers of ghost guns, to ban the company from selling and marketing its products to consumers in violation of District of Columbia law. This is a clear example of how, even when legislatures fail and law enforcement has no clear policy to enforce, executive and judicial action can still help protect people from gun crime. This, too, is popular - 70% of Virginians and even 69% of Republicans support limits on the spread of ghost guns.
Virginia needs legislation, law enforcement expertise, and executive and judicial action to achieve gun safety. This will let us achieve the goals a bipartisan majority of Virginians support, including enhanced background checks and a ban on ghost guns. The costs of gun violence couldn’t be clearer. Virginians desperately want action to make Virginia safer. We need leadership to help make our communities safer and enact laws to encourage responsible gun ownership. Virginians overwhelmingly support these policies and expect their leaders to, as well.
The Richmond Times-Dispatch: VanValkenburg and Jones: Virginians Support Common Sense Gun Reform - Our Leaders Should Too [https://act.myngp.com/el/YZ69X0SdipjbRu_WKsqG4x3YmNFnLeZ4UC_orj9guj4=/https://richmond.com/opinion/column/virginians-support-gun-reform-leaders-should-too/article_0b3c0dbc-2cc7-11ef-8ebe-a36bff86f08a.html=]
Consider the horror of a few simple statistics: between 2016 and 2022, an average of 3 Virginians died by firearm each day [https://www.vdh.virginia.gov/firearm-injury/#:~:text=Virginia%20Firearm%20Injury%20Fast%20Facts,followed%20by%20homicide%20(36%25).] . In 2022 alone, Virginians spent 7,000 days hospitalized for nonfatal firearm injuries, with over $136 million in hospitalization costs [https://www.vdh.virginia.gov/firearm-injury/#:~:text=Virginia%20Firearm%20Injury%20Fast%20Facts,followed%20by%20homicide%20(36%25).] . This data, provided by the Virginia Department of Health, are alarming, disappointing, and somehow unsurprising all at once.
Why unsurprising? Because we know that gun violence remains a scourge on Virginia communities, from Norfolk to Henrico to Lee County and everywhere in between. Recognizing that fact, in 2020, the General Assembly, led by Democrats in both houses, passed several long-stifled measures aimed at curbing gun violence throughout the Commonwealth. Governor Northam signed [https://www.cnn.com/2020/04/10/politics/ralph-northam-signs-gun-bills/index.html] a red flag law, limited the number of handguns purchasable per month, and policies to ensure lost and stolen firearms were swiftly reported to law enforcement. Since the election of a divided government three years ago, though, progress on such far-sighted measures has stalled.
Nonetheless, common ground can be found to keep Virginians safe. This year Senator VanValkenburg carried and passed Lucia’s Law [https://www.wric.com/news/politics/capitol-connection/lucias-law-signed-on-the-3rd-anniversary-of-henrico-13-year-olds-murder/] , a bill that holds irresponsible gun owners accountable when they let guns fall into the hands of minors who are known to be a risk to themselves or others. This common sense measure received bipartisan support in the House and Senate and was signed by the Governor.
Despite that one victory, and the ongoing pain gun violence inflicts on Virginians, Republicans in the House of Delegates attempted to repeal every single common sense gun safety law in 2022 and 2023. They persisted in these efforts to roll back the progress made in 2020 despite wide support for firearm safety measures in Virginia. For example, 73% of Virginians [https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/ifar4p4udsv6rolm3nows/Everytown-Memo-VA-Poll-Results.docx?rlkey=3kf0fy5quworxv2x57qy1r9t4&e=1&dl=0] support enhanced background checks and a requirement to securely store firearms. That’s a bipartisan group, too - 62% of Republicans agree on enhanced background checks and 56% of Republicans with safe storage requirements. When the legislature was able to pass bipartisan gun violence prevention legislation reflecting this public consensus, Governor Youngkin sided with extremists and vetoed the overwhelming majority of the bills.
But it’s not just about legislation. Lucia’s Law and other gun safety measures need vigorous implementation by law enforcement to be successful. Indeed, these laws all contain provisions giving law enforcement agencies an important role to play in figuring out how to effectively enforce the new policies. Collaboration between legislators and law enforcement experts is critical in our effort to build a safer Virginia rooted in common sense principles of safety, which is preferred by a majority [https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/ifar4p4udsv6rolm3nows/Everytown-Memo-VA-Poll-Results.docx?rlkey=3kf0fy5quworxv2x57qy1r9t4&e=1&dl=0] of Virginians.
There is a third pillar to support effective gun safety efforts: the need for executive officials to act on their own. When the Governor stifles gun violence prevention and the agencies lack policies to implement, it becomes the responsibility of other executive officials to act.
As an example, legislation regulating “ghost guns,” firearms that are easily assembled and lack serial numbers, was vetoed last month. Ghost guns can be purchased without a background check, making it easier for these weapons to fall into the hands of bad actors. Former Delegate Jones was part of the team that successfully sued [https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2022/08/11/dc-ghost-guns-polymer80-judgment/] Polymer80, one of the nation’s largest manufacturers of ghost guns, to ban the company from selling and marketing its products to consumers in violation of District of Columbia law. This is a clear example of how, even when legislatures fail and law enforcement has no clear policy to enforce, executive and judicial action can still help protect people from gun crime. This, too, is popular - 70% of Virginians and even 69% of Republicans support limits on the spread of ghost guns.
Virginia needs all three pillars to achieve gun safety: legislation, law enforcement expertise, and executive and judicial action. This will let us achieve the goals a bipartisan majority of Virginians support, including enhanced background checks and a ban on ghost guns. The costs of gun violence couldn’t be clearer. Virginians desperately want action to make Virginia safer. We need leadership to help make our communities safer and enact laws to encourage responsible gun ownership. Virginians overwhelmingly support these policies and expect their leaders to, as well.
- Jay

name: PoliticsPA
subject: Game changer for cashless payments in PA
body:
| | | |
---
| | | Welcome to the latest edition of _Voice of Reason_ where we’ll recap exclusive news and data featured in our most recent podcast.

The segment focused on the proposed ban on swipe fees from the sales tax portion of transactions, which risks disrupting the electronic payment system that guards your credit and debit cards in PA.

Two issue experts, Kevin Shivers and Christina Mihalik, joined us to share their views and insights you want to know.
---
| **Big Names Make News**
---
| **CEO of the PA Association of Community Bankers Kevin Shivers** compared electronic payment interchange fees to paying the USPS to deliver your taxes. "There's a cost to running the system to administer the safe, secure, convenient way of conducting electronic transactions." [[Watch](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=a4bfe6c358&e=b7b3eddce2)]

**Senior V.P. for Gov't Relations with CrossState Credit Union Assoc. Christina Mihalik** explained that underserved communities relying on community banks are most affected by the dismantling of the interchange system because they have to cover the gaps left by the removal of fees with their own money. [[Watch](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=06dffda909&e=b7b3eddce2)]
---
|
* * *
---
| **Why It Matters**
---
| _Small Business_
* Many small businesses simply cannot afford to upgrade their technology to accommodate a new payment system, leading them to **potentially reject card payments altogether**. This would drive consumers into "big box" stores instead. [[Watch](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=20ee2a48a7&e=b7b3eddce2)]

_Inefficiency_
* Neither the software nor hardware exists to safely and efficiently separate out sales tax from the underlying cost of goods or services sold, meaning** consumers might have to pay the sales tax portion of their purchases in cash**. [[Watch](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=e9cd0c8c82&e=b7b3eddce2)]

_Consumer Privacy_
* By banning swipe fees on sales tax, **government would have the ability to "look inside consumers' shopping carts"** to breakdown which items are subject to sales tax and which are not, as opposed to secure payment systems only looking at the total cost. [[Watch](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=d26368d271&e=b7b3eddce2)]

---
|
* * *
---
| **Game Changing Proposal Could Disrupt How You Use Your Credit Cards in PA**
---
| [ ](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=68283e742f&e=b7b3eddce2 "Top Policy Proposals to Watch in PA’s Budget Battle | Voices of Reason Ep. 7")
---
Proposals to exclude fees from the sales tax portion of transactions would disrupt funding for fraud prevention, card statements, customer service, credit monitoring, and more.
|

---
| [ ](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=879a3f3847&e=b7b3eddce2)

|
* * *
---
| **In Case You Missed It**
---
| PoliticsPA was **live on-site at the Harrisburg rotunda** earlier this week recording our signature podcast, _Voices of Reason_.

_Voices of Reason_ has covered the most important issues in Pennsylvania politics – from [education funding](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=4858e48f5c&e=b7b3eddce2) to [trust in elections](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=4ee0c4ebca&e=b7b3eddce2). Secretary of the Commonwealth [Al Schmidt](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=4b84b0af66&e=b7b3eddce2), PA Treasurer [Stacy Garrity](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=86ef31508f&e=b7b3eddce2), and House Appropriations Chairman [Jordan Harris](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=33b34e14e0&e=b7b3eddce2) are just a few of many influential guests who have joined us for exclusive interviews and roundtable discussions.

name: The New Pennsylvania Project
subject: Your Bi-Weekly NPP eBlast
body:
| | |
---
Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New Pennsylvania Project newsletter! In this edition, you'll find critical election news, updates on upcoming and recent events, and exciting career opportunities. We’re here to keep you informed about our progress in breaking down voting barriers, key election updates, and the initiatives shaping Pennsylvania's future.

We also address how unfair the proposed Pennsylvania budget is and how it threatens to direct funding away from our communities so the rich can get richer. This budget and the headlines in the news are a reminder of why we must continue our efforts at all levels—on the streets and in the courts—to protect our rights and our communities. Freedom and liberation are projects in progress, not a destination we have reached.
As we gear up for the 2024 general election, we invite you to join us in our mission to educate and mobilize voters who then vote every election to make change in our communities. Stay informed with essential election resources and dates as we approach the 2024 General Election on November 5th.

Remember, your voice matters, and we’re here to provide the information and resources needed to shape Pennsylvania’s future.

Thank you for staying informed and engaged! Together, change is possible.
---
| | |
---
---
**Unreasonable Podcast "Engaging the Politically Unengaged" with Kadida Kenner**
---
---
The New Pennsylvania Project’s CEO, Kadida Kenner, is featured on the latest episode of the Unreasonable podcast: "Engaging the Politically Unengaged."
Kadida shares insights about our mission to engage and register voters in underserved impacted communities. Don't miss her important perspective on the current mindset of voters, especially minority voters under 35.

**Celebrating Juneteenth** Since our last newsletter Juneteenth took place. It is an important celebration in the communities centered by the New Pennsylvania Project that we could not let the day pass without recognition. Juneteenth is a reminder of where we have come from and the path ahead of us to be fully free and secure in our rights. It is a day that marks the end of chattel slavery in the United States and celebrates the resilience, strength, and leadership of Black people.
It is also more than a historical milestone; it’s a reminder of the ongoing fight for justice and equality. We recognize the incredible contributions of Black leaders who have paved the way and continue to inspire us in the struggle for civil rights - including our voting rights.At the New Pennsylvania Project, we stand with the Black community and all those committed to fighting for freedom and equity. We are committed to amplifying voices and ensuring that every eligible voter has the opportunity to be heard.

In that spirit we would like to lift up one story of a woman’s decade long fight to make Juneteenth a U.S. holiday. Opal Lee, “has become known as the Grandmother of Juneteenth. Her annual walks culminated in a trip to the Capitol in September, carrying a petition signed by 11⁄2 million Americans urging Congress to pass legislation for a federal holiday. To read more about Opal click here.

Let's celebrate the progress we've made and continue to push for a brighter, more equitable future for all.

clean_body: | | | Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New Pennsylvania Project newsletter! In this edition, you'll find critical election news, updates on upcoming and recent events, and exciting career opportunities. We’re here to keep you informed about our progress in breaking down voting barriers, key election updates, and the initiatives shaping Pennsylvania's future. We also address how unfair the proposed Pennsylvania budget is and how it threatens to direct funding away from our communities so the rich can get richer. This budget and the headlines in the news are a reminder of why we must continue our efforts at all levels—on the streets and in the courts—to protect our rights and our communities. Freedom and liberation are projects in progress, not a destination we have reached. As we gear up for the 2024 general election, we invite you to join us in our mission to educate and mobilize voters who then vote every election to make change in our communities. Stay informed with essential election resources and dates as we approach the 2024 General Election on November 5th. Remember, your voice matters, and we’re here to provide the information and resources needed to shape Pennsylvania’s future. Thank you for staying informed and engaged! Together, change is possible. | | | Unreasonable Podcast "Engaging the Politically Unengaged" with Kadida Kenner The New Pennsylvania Project’s CEO, Kadida Kenner, is featured on the latest episode of the Unreasonable podcast: "Engaging the Politically Unengaged." Kadida shares insights about our mission to engage and register voters in underserved impacted communities. Don't miss her important perspective on the current mindset of voters, especially minority voters under 35. Tune in and get inspired to get involved! The 2024 Pennsylvania Forty Under 40: Meet some of the state’s most influential millennials “Since 2020, Abbott has built a 12-person staff and a coalition that includes public-interest stalwarts like Planned Parenthood, Conservation Voters of Pennsylvania, The New Pennsylvania Project and various labor unions. “I love working with people on the frontlines of trying to make their communities better,” says Abbott. “They’re not just doing political work; they’re making a social impact.” | Celebrating Juneteenth Since our last newsletter Juneteenth took place. It is an important celebration in the communities centered by the New Pennsylvania Project that we could not let the day pass without recognition. Juneteenth is a reminder of where we have come from and the path ahead of us to be fully free and secure in our rights. It is a day that marks the end of chattel slavery in the United States and celebrates the resilience, strength, and leadership of Black people. It is also more than a historical milestone; it’s a reminder of the ongoing fight for justice and equality. We recognize the incredible contributions of Black leaders who have paved the way and continue to inspire us in the struggle for civil rights - including our voting rights.At the New Pennsylvania Project, we stand with the Black community and all those committed to fighting for freedom and equity. We are committed to amplifying voices and ensuring that every eligible voter has the opportunity to be heard. In that spirit we would like to lift up one story of a woman’s decade long fight to make Juneteenth a U.S. holiday. Opal Lee, “has become known as the Grandmother of Juneteenth. Her annual walks culminated in a trip to the Capitol in September, carrying a petition signed by 11⁄2 million Americans urging Congress to pass legislation for a federal holiday. To read more about Opal click here. Let's celebrate the progress we've made and continue to push for a brighter, more equitable future for all. | Are You Ready for the Presidential Debate! On Thursday, June 27th, the stage is set for the first presidential debate of the 2024 general election.This is your chance to hear directly from the candidates about their plans and visions for our future. Debates are an important part of our democracy, helping us make informed choices about who should represent us. Tune in, listen carefully, and take notes on the issues that matter most to you and your community. You can view the debate WHYY-TV 12 & livestreaming at whyy.org/tv PBS will provide live coverage and analysis of the debate by Amna Nawaz and Geoff Bennett. Remember, your voice and vote are powerful tools for change. Let’s stay informed, engaged, and ready to make a difference! | 2024 US Election Guide: Comprehensive Voter Information In 2024, your vote will shape the future of our communities.There is so much misinformation and intentional disinformation out there. The New Pennsylvania Project believes all voters should be informed when they go to vote and we are happy to provide voters with the information they need to make decisions that will impact their lives, family, and community. When we vote, we win! | | | | | | We're Hiring! Join the New Pennsylvania Project (NPP) and be a part of our mission to empower impacted, Black and other communities of color across PA. Help us support every eligible voter to feel compelled to vote. Your work will make a direct impact on civil rights, fair education funding, economic justice, and environmental stewardship. | | | | | | 2024 State of Black Pittsburgh: Housing Stability, Electoral Impact On Thursday (6/27) Kadida Kenner, CEO of the New Pennsylvania Project, spoke at the University of Pittsburgh for a very important event, "2024 State of Black Pittsburgh: Housing Stability, Electoral Impact." Black voter participation is key to driving real change in our communities, especially on important issues like housing stability and ensuring policies that improve everyday life. Black voters will shape the future of Pittsburgh and Pennsylvania. | | | | | | | | | | Partisan gridlock prevents fixes to Pennsylvania’s voting laws as presidential election looms “Pennsylvania is seeing lots of action targeting gaps in its vote-by-mail laws. The problem is that it’s in the courtroom and not the legislature. That could make the most populous presidential swing state a hotbed of challenges and conspiracy theories if the November election is close, as expected.” Read more in The Lawsuit to Protect Thousands of Pennsylvania Voters “For thousands of voters in every election, an error on a meaningless requirement has meant that their ballots have been disqualified. Trivial errors on the ballot return envelopes, like not including a handwritten date on the outer return envelope, led to more than 10,000 uncounted votes in the 2022 election alone.” . Updates on Pennsylvania's Election Lawsuits “There is more active election litigation in Pennsylvania than any other state (or commonwealth). Marc and Paige break down the 14 lawsuits in the Keystone State and how they could affect voters this fall.” On May 28th our friends at the New PA Project Education Fund, alongside other advocacy groups, filed a lawsuit to challenge Pennsylvania's rejection of mail-in ballots due to minor date errors on ballot envelopes. The RNC and DNC have both sought to intervene in the case, indicating its significance. This from Democracy Docket linked here explains the importance of this lawsuit and others in Pennsylvania. | ‘It’s his DACA moment’: Advocates ecstatic over Biden immigration plan “We know that Pennsylvania is going to make or break the election, and we’re here as CASA in Action because we are getting ready for a major electoral voter mobilization program, and the Latino community needs to know that Biden’s promise to keep families together — he is actively working on that and moving forward with this executive order that’s going to affect so many people around the country,” said Jossie Flor Sapunar, national communications director for CASA in Action, the political wing of an immigration advocacy group in Pennsylvania, Virginia and Maryland.” Will legal weed be part of the PA’s 2024 budget? “Reaching a consensus in the closely divided state House is only the first hurdle for legalization. The next — and much bigger one — would be winning over the Republican-controlled state Senate. Legislative Republicans have long blocked action on cannabis by citing its federal status as a Schedule I drug, which the Drug Enforcement Administration says has “no currently accepted medical use and a high potential for abuse.” President Biden’s “Parole in Place” Program Is Popular With Voters “Last Tuesday, President Biden announced a new “Parole in Place” immigration program, which will offer work permits, protection from deportation, and a streamlined path to citizenship for about 500,000 eligible undocumented immigrants....In a new survey, Data for Progress finds that 63% of voters — including 85% of Democrats, 58% of Independents, and 40% of Republicans — support the Parole in Place initiative.” PA Latino Voters Speak Out On Immigration, Border Issues. “Latino/a voters in Pennsylvania in the survey prefer President Joe Biden over former President Donald Trump on immigration by seven points (39-32%) – a difference that is smaller than Nevada’s 19-point separation.” . Division Over School Vouchers Muddies Education Spending In PA Budget Talks. “While Pennsylvania's school voucher proposal is targeted to the 15% worst performing schools many of which serve a majority or near majority of Black and brown students, many Black or brown legislators and others who represent them stand opposed to vouchers.” Legislation banning foreign influence through dark money passes Pa. House committee The State Government Committee approved the legislation on Monday, and supporters hope it will soon hit the House floor for a full vote. Pennsylvania has some of the loosest campaign finance laws in the country, shown in comparisons to other states by the National Conference of State Legislatures. People and committees can spend unlimited amounts of money in political contributions. . [] Like us, the voters of Missouri’s 1st Congressional District know that Cori will always advocate for the needs of our community. She has fought tirelessly to bring much-needed resources and attention to our district. She has been a fierce advocate for justice and equity, ensuring that the voices of the marginalized are heard in the halls of power. Her work has brought hope and tangible progress to our community. St. Louis and its people are stronger than ever. But now, that progress is under threat. GOP megadonors are pouring money into our race, trying to buy this seat and deliver on their extremist agenda. If they succeed, everything we’ve fought for will be at risk. So, Peter, can we count on you to donate to our campaign today? [] If you have saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: DONATE $5 [] DONATE $10 [] DONATE $25 [] DONATE $50 [] DONATE $100 [] OTHER [] These megadonors want to turn back the clock on the progress we’ve made, reverting St. Louis to a time of neglect and injustice. We can’t – we WON’T – let that happen. Thanks, Devon Moody, Campaign Manager [] As a frontline Ferguson activist, a formerly unhoused single mother of two, a nurse, a survivor, and a pastor, Congresswoman Cori Bush knows the struggles our communities face on a daily basis. In 2020, on a mission to save lives, she defeated a 52-year political dynasty; in 2022, St. Louis sent her back to Congress with a strong mandate to champion racial, economic, reproductive, gender, health, and environmental justice. Now, Cori is running for re-election to continue doing the most for everyone, starting with those who have the greatest need. | | Peter, I hope you’re enjoying your final Friday in June. We’ve had a very special Pride Month here in IL-17. I got to walk in my hometown’s first ever Pride Parade! It was pretty special marching down Rockford’s State Street, with tons of people lining the streets, even in the pouring rain! A onversation with one young man was particularly special, and will stay with me for a long time. He said to me, “You came to my school as our weatherman and I knew you were gay and you helped me be myself. When I saw you run for Congress and win? I knew I wanted to follow in your footsteps!” And THAT, Peter, means as much to me as anything. I love celebrating Pride Month with events and parades, but stories like this one shows that this time of year is about the generations of children in Illinois who will see themselves represented in their own hometowns, whoever they are. Every young child deserves to knows that they can be _themselves_ and still thrive – and lead – in our communities. Talking to that young man, I saw the next generation of Rockford leaders. I am so proud to be Illinois’ first out Member of Congress, and I am going to work tirelessly to make sure I am not the last. That starts with our election this November. [**We need to hold this seat to continue making our community better for ALL of our neighbors, and that means raising enough to fend off extremist Republican attacks. clean_body: Friend, I hope you’re enjoying your final Friday in June. ~ | | Peter, I hope you’re enjoying your final Friday in June. We’ve had a very special Pride Month here in IL-17. I got to walk in my hometown’s first ever Pride Parade! It was pretty special marching down Rockford’s State Street, with tons of people lining the streets, even in the pouring rain! A onversation with one young man was particularly special, and will stay with me for a long time. He said to me, “You came to my school as our weatherman and I knew you were gay and you helped me be myself. When I saw you run for Congress and win? I knew I wanted to follow in your footsteps!” And THAT, Peter, means as much to me as anything. I love celebrating Pride Month with events and parades, but stories like this one shows that this time of year is about the generations of children in Illinois who will see themselves represented in their own hometowns, whoever they are. Every young child deserves to knows that they can be themselves and still thrive – and lead – in our communities. Talking to that young man, I saw the next generation of Rockford leaders. I am so proud to be Illinois’ first out Member of Congress, and I am going to work tirelessly to make sure I am not the last. That starts with our election this November. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:____ | **~~ | ~~ ---|--- ~~ | ~ ~ | Once again, Peter, Happy Pride. subject: Respectfully asking if you can chip in $5
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
#
]
Hey there, Peter. It’s Ruben.
[**I’m reaching out to respectfully ask if you can make a $5 donation to my campaign before our FEC reporting deadline hits at midnight on Sunday.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-june24.NmHAEe&amount=5&refcode=em240628-2-160&t=1&akid=2545%2E734936%2EX8dFGf)
This request is coming at a really intense moment — both for me and for our campaign. Please, let me explain what I mean by that:
Right around this time last year I was getting ready to take some time off the campaign trail. My baby girl Isla was about to be born and I wasn’t going to miss those first few weeks for anything. Not after the way I grew up, after my dad left our family. Close to a year later, I can’t believe how much she’s grown.

I want to tell you about something other candidates won't admit:
How we choose to fund our campaign influences more than just how we pay for staff, ads, and organizing. It has a direct impact on both our message and who we actually serve in office. Any politician or pundit who tells you otherwise is lying -- and I have the receipts to prove it.
Despite virtually every member of Congress having campaigned on making life-saving drugs more accessible, politicians who take millions of dollars from Big Pharma are still telling us we have to accept a world where people die because they have to ration their medicine.
Then we have out-of-touch elites like Josh Hawley, who have spent decades wasting our money on tax breaks and subsidies for Wall Street, Big Pharma, Big Tech, and just about everything else that's gutting our country -- all while refusing to invest even a penny back into the state they were elected to represent.
They're willing to lie, cheat, and steal from the American people to protect the corporate PACs and mega-donors who own them -- and they'll even raise their fist to look strong before they start running from threats to our democracy.
We don't need any more liars or frauds like Josh Hawley in Congress.**** That's why I'm running for U.S. Senate. It's why I'm not taking a single cent from corporate PACs. And it's why I've relied on real people like you to build this movement since Day One -- not federal lobbyists, national insiders, or Big Oil or Big Pharma execs.
That commitment to running this campaign the right way has given us the ability to run the boldest campaign in Missouri history -- taking on corrupt political elites like Hawley without hesitation about some mega-donor being upset. And our mission of taking power back for everyday people has earned our movement national media attention.
More than just banning insider trading among members of Congress and their families --**I 'm running to put them in jail if they steal from us.**
More than just breaking up Big Pharma --**I 'm running to prosecute the insulin cartels who are killing people.**
More than just fighting to codify protections for abortion access -- **I 'm running to end the filibuster so we can actually get it done.**
And more than just rejecting corporate PAC money -- **I 'm running to abolish corporate PACs altogether.**
This campaign is powered by the people because that's exactly who I'll work for in the U.S. Senate -- I'll be accountable to real, everyday Americans, not some corporate executive or political machine. We're throwing out their rulebook and building a grassroots movement to fundamentally change who has power in our country. And I want you to be part of it.
**So if you 're ready to help us defeat Josh Hawley and give Missouri's U.S. Senate seat back to everyday people, please add a donation of whatever you can before our end-of-quarter fundraising deadline on June 30th.**

In our efforts to show our Senators how much a national monument for the Owyhee Canyonlands means to us, we are starting an Owyhee art contest! **This contest is open to anyone of any skill level and age.** We accept any form of art as well, whether painting, drawing, or poetry. You are not required to live in Oregon to enter, as we recognize that anyone can appreciate the Owyhee Canyonlands. There will be two categories for winners, one for youth (under 18) and one for adults (over 18).**Both of the winning pieces will be presented to Senator Wyden, in addition to being featured on our website.** **Ready to submit?** Take a photo of your artwork and submit it one of these two ways:
1. Post your artwork on social media and use the hashtag #ProtectTheOwyhee and tag OLCV! (Twitter: @olcv | Facebook: @oregonlcv | Instagram: @olcv)
2. [Use this google form to upload your artwork and we will share it on social media for you](https://click.everyaction.com/k/87793485/482283675/-1078088021?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjRjNzhlMmIzLTZiMzUtZWYxMS04NmQyLTYwNDViZGQ5ZTA5NiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=rwdUGnLtwga3-6EAhTdLtUWHoeqCRRfg5t-mXMrRMh8=&emci=fb5f4ec0-bd34-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=4c78e2b3-6b35-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=2107230)

In order to be eligible to win, you must share your name and date of birth. It is optional, but greatly welcomed, to share where you are from. Either way you choose to submit, you are encouraged to share about your artwork and tell us what the Owyhee Canyonlands mean to you - although it is not required to enter. T**he deadline for submissions is Monday, September 2nd** , and the winner will be announced shortly after. [**Don’t miss this opportunity to create fun art for a magical place and show our Senators how much we want to protect the Owyhee Canyonlands!**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/87793486/482283676/-1078088021?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjRjNzhlMmIzLTZiMzUtZWYxMS04NmQyLTYwNDViZGQ5ZTA5NiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=rwdUGnLtwga3-6EAhTdLtUWHoeqCRRfg5t-mXMrRMh8=&emci=fb5f4ec0-bd34-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=4c78e2b3-6b35-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=2107230) I’m excited to see what you create. | | _**Let's Get to Work!**_
---
| | Friends, My name is Randy Head, I am the new Indiana Republican Party Chair. I am beyond honored to serve in this capacity and I cannot wait to get to work with our amazing team and grassroots leaders to continue the storied success that the Republican Party has achieved over the course of the last 20 years. It is important to our team that we continue to engage our grassroots and be a resource for all of you out there doing the work to get Republicans elected up and down the ballot. The first step to getting to know all of you, is to introduce myself. I am an attorney from Logansport, Indiana. I have served as a precinct committeeman, state delegate, county chair, county prosecutor, and state senator. I tell you this to let you know that I believe in serving our party and I will never ask you to do anything I haven't already done myself. I would also like to introduce our new Executive Director, Josh Waddell. Josh started his electoral campaigning career early at the age of 13, volunteering for the Indiana Republican Party. He has worked in Indiana politics ever since, including working for Congressman Trey Hollingsworth, Senator Todd Young, Senator Mike Braun, and as the Clark County Republican Party Secretary. I am excited to work with Josh to make sure the Indiana Republican Party continues our streak of success. Thank you all for welcoming me over the last week. I am very excited about the state of our party and to be able to serve all of you. Let's get to work and win big in November!
---
| |
---
| | Chairman Randy Head

She has consistently supported these extreme measures, demonstrating a complete disregard for women's autonomy and health. **As your representative, I will fight tirelessly to protect reproductive rights and ensure that all women have the freedom to make their own healthcare decisions. This cannot stand.**

**What is Project 2025? The ‘dystopian’ manifesto for Trump’s second term**
— The Independent, June 2024 Friend, Donald Trump’s allies are hell-bent on taking away our freedoms. Here’s what they have in store for Donald Trump’s first six months if he’s elected president again: Defunding the Department of Justice. Dismantling the FBI and Homeland Security. Firing government officials who aren’t loyal to Donald Trump. Abolishing the Department of Education. Removing abortion pills from the market. Rejecting abortion as health care. | | | [ ](https://www.jillstein2024.com/donate?e=e813143e1dc0d3b0ffcb007ffe357333&utm_source=jillsteinforpresident&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=biden_is_toast&n=1)

Peter, Let’s talk about last night. CNN held a rigged debate intended to protect the duopoly by keeping competitors like us off the stage. Then the debate started. By the end of those torturous 90 minutes, the universal reaction was clear: [** _‘Biden is toast’_**](https://www.jillstein2024.com/r?u=Qj32F8ZTIcBOzthgR25-gAvkYhzfYdFFirPiGZztCb0&e=e813143e1dc0d3b0ffcb007ffe357333&utm_source=jillsteinforpresident&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=biden_is_toast&n=2)
---
[ ](www.jillstein2024.com/donate)
---
Biden’s disastrous performance puts into question his ability to even serve out the remainder of his current term – let alone another four years. The dishonesty of Democrats about Biden’s clear limitations will end up being the true spoiler in this election. Meanwhile, Trump steamrolled the moderators with a predictable, unchecked stream of lies, racism, and calls to violence.

**This debate was embarrassing. Worse, it was dangerous.** Both of these men are fundamentally unfit to serve and neither can be allowed a second term in the White House. No one there was willing to fight for the truth. Not one candidate or moderator.

_**[The media gave up and the empire’s facade collapsed on national television.](https://www.jillstein2024.com/r?u=Qj32F8ZTIcBOzthgR25-gAvkYhzfYdFFirPiGZztCb0&e=e813143e1dc0d3b0ffcb007ffe357333&utm_source=jillsteinforpresident&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=biden_is_toast&n=3)**_

We deserve better than what happened last night. We deserve a real debate with candidates willing and able to discuss our future. We deserve a real contest of ideas and leaders with vision.

In the wake of this embarrassing debacle, voters are already seeking out new options for November. Our campaign, already on the ballot for the majority of voters, is the obvious choice.

That’s why we need your support to let the American people know that Jill is the only pro-worker, anti-genocide, climate action candidate with a path to the White House.

** _Peter, will you help Jill give the American people a real alternative on the ballot across the nation by making a contribution of any amount right now?_****_

I want to share how far we've come, but first, I have to ask: = | = Only three Black women have come before me to earn this honor, so I'm facing one of the largest glass ceilings in American politics. But I'm no stranger to tough fights. With the support of this grassroots team, I became the first woman and person of color to represent Delaware in the House. Now, I'm running to make history again in the Senate. Despite the many barriers that stand in my way, I know I can get there, but it'll only happen with the support of people like you. I'll tell you why: Historically, Black women running for office only raise one-third of what their white counterparts do. And already, I've seen that painful statistic come to life. My self-funding opponent has already written his campaign a check for nearly a million dollars of his own personal fortune. That means we're heading into our LAST FEC deadline before the primary election with some serious ground to make up. Several brave Americans, led by Black and Brown trans activists, fought back against police violence and harassment. Demonstrations throughout the city happened over the span of six days, kickstarting the modern LGBTQ+ movement for equal rights. Stonewall is a story of those who came before us and put everything on the line in a demand to be treated with dignity and respect. Those who bravely stood up and spoke out so that others wouldn’t have to live in fear or silence. Progress was made possible by the Black and Brown trans activists who have always been on the frontlines of the fight for LGBTQ+ rights. We must never forget that. I’m inspired by how far we’ve come in the past 55 years, but as Republicans continue their assault on LGBTQ+ rights — targeting and dehumanizing trans kids, banning LGBTQ+ discussion in our schools, and even threatening to overturn Supreme Court decisions that granted our right to marriage equality — it’s clear there is so much more work to be done. It’s going to take all of us to counter these right wing attacks and ensure LGBTQ+ Americans across the country are given the support and equal opportunities they deserve. **[Will you join me in this fight to protect and advance the progress we’ve made by making a donation to my reelection campaign today? Dear Peter,
In Washington's 8th Congressional District, we believe that every voice matters and deserves to be heard. Our campaign is dedicated to amplifying the concerns, ideas, and aspirations of our community, ensuring they are represented and respected in our nation's capital.
From town halls to community forums, we have been actively listening to your stories and understanding the issues that matter most to you. Whether it's advocating for lower taxes, protecting our liberties, or supporting local businesses, your voice guides our mission and fuels our dedication.
To continue this important work, we need your support.

---

|
Your contribution will help us reach more voters, host more events, and keep our community engaged and informed. Every dollar you give amplifies the voice of our district and strengthens our collective impact.
Join us in making sure that Washington's 8th District is heard loud and clear. Your donation, whether it’s $20, $50, or any amount, will make a significant difference.

Dear Peter,
Can you keep a secret? Tobias’ birthday is Monday, July 1st, and I’d love to surprise him with a card full of messages from his friends and supporters! Tobias has worked tirelessly for Oregonians, and I know that seeing your name on his birthday card would mean the world to him.
Tobias has been a dedicated advocate for all Oregonians, championing and implementing innovative programs to help open up pathways to allow people to achieve their full potential. He’s running for Secretary of State because the power to vote is critical to everything else we want to achieve, allowing us to help determine the direction we want Oregon to take. Tobias will protect and defend this right—what a contrast to his Republican opponent, who took a case all the way to the U.S. Supreme Court trying to get rid of vote by mail!
Tobias has long been on the front lines fighting for our values. Now, it’s our turn to show him how much we appreciate his unwavering commitment.
Please take a moment to leave him a birthday message (no donation required!):

| **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

Peter, can the government pass a law that makes someone good? For so long, we knew the answer to that question, but it seems as though we have forgotten. Sometimes we think we need a law to compel people to be better, that if another law is put on the books, suddenly others will develop a strong sense of right and wrong. That’s not the case though. **__[You have to decide that on your own.](http://links.redconservatives.com/u/click?_t=66ce1250519441959ebe70cf27686494&_m=17ec39ad7f814bf098d6906b9bce5ee6&_e=3EdHXUOZQBwtI2xOMgfiypZVcIRT1UwfcTDV7Ya7PBlHArvXk1UAYEnh8r_Qs76UFNBG2qpOUmmksRpA0u1kn4au_GhBYBnjyYmckKlF1h-cigwajB996a2Mt-XnpIaX4nNFeByPRrXEa6d4ufAcdQHgXavZZ1FnHSs8_Vm3S-SF7OElYjN5d0z3ILqRjvE7oCK1qKajETmns_YLZY8nT_rPW0o7Lh2OeVph5lkMijEqix294NzNiWMu4_31njqmsTW2uFNV7a258sKut9D0_DlLGdpY1Rm6WMUTbJFlHi8tN9qkjxH-WCkgfRjtSgJppo5KY_CfRmznXSp78QQg_JTkB0W6Y-jswabvNYXoM-SW4AYV63vTy21UJtdfOlbrtLaf1Q4_cuViKoEphFj-gvmB5nKF0jJSB8s6Vd0D3KY%3D)_ _** The answer to life’s toughest questions **never** comes from the government. They come from God, from our neighbors, from our family, from our pastors setting an example for us. All of this comes down to the same basic principle of right vs. wrong and good vs. evil. That moral compass and being guided by faith have shaped our country since its founding. It’s ingrained in who we are, what we value, and why we fight so hard to preserve and protect liberty. Because liberty is tied directly to what we value and the idea that people are inherently good and have a sense of morality. Somewhere over time, our country lost its moral compass and deep faith. Instead of turning to God to guide us, many Americans have looked to the government for those teachings and guidance. Protecting liberty and freedom starts with reminding our fellow Americans that our rights come from above, not the government... **because liberty and freedom are a beautiful thing. ** It’s even more beautiful when people come together to do good in their communities, to live by their faith, and not look to the government to teach them what they can and should value. Peter, my goal has _always_ been to fight for the values you and I share, to protect liberty for the next generation. **At a time when the Swamp diminishes those who walk by faith and bill Big Government as the solution to all of our problems, it’s more imperative than ever that we stand together to protect freedom.** _**[**Will you chip in $10, $20, $25, $50, or whatever you can afford to stand with me in this fight to preserve liberty and freedom for the next generation?**](http://links.redconservatives.com/u/click?_t=66ce1250519441959ebe70cf27686494&_m=17ec39ad7f814bf098d6906b9bce5ee6&_e=3EdHXUOZQBwtI2xOMgfiypZVcIRT1UwfcTDV7Ya7PBlHArvXk1UAYEnh8r_Qs76UFNBG2qpOUmmksRpA0u1kn4au_GhBYBnjyYmckKlF1h-cigwajB996a2Mt-XnpIaX4nNFeByPRrXEa6d4ufAcdQHgXavZZ1FnHSs8_Vm3S-SF7OElYjN5d0z3ILqRjvE7oCK1qKajETmns_YLZY8nT_rPW0o7Lh2OeVph5lkMijEqix294NzNiWMu4_31njqmsTW2uFNV7a258sKut9D0_H06dDbucDyYrVFcfgS6PCwyLb7G7AEMrLofqW9rWUfDhZ5c0urnqNQuzbSdNeVaokjr2PyEoP2F16UWRqbfTH8a4YaeCDks1lp0mzFEfaoKwkPTWkxQkUWPHE-ba5dnGY7WAl8zudb0S52DxMyAS3s%3D)**_

Can I tell you the story of how I first got involved in politics, Peter? When my boys were young, my husband and I were both working full-time. I worked the night shift at the Chapel Hill Police Department, would get off work at 7am and go straight to their classrooms to volunteer. Throughout this experience I discovered that kids, especially Black and brown kids, were being underserved. **When I could do nothing more as a volunteer, I ran for School Board.** During my time on the school board, I fought for better funding for our schools. I felt that the county was not adequately funding schools, so because **I could do nothing more on the School Board, I ran for Orange County Commissioner.** During my time as County Commissioner, I championed the construction of two schools, two senior centers, affordable housing initiatives, and more. Eventually, I reached a point where **I could do nothing more as County Commissioner, so I ran for State House.** Are you sensing a theme, Peter? I got into this line of work in pursuit of building a better life for my community — **and there is still SO much more I can do.** [That’s why I’m running for re-election. clean_body: Can I tell you the story of how I first got involved in politics? If you’d like to unsubscribe, | | Can I tell you the story of how I first got involved in politics, Peter? When my boys were young, my husband and I were both working full-time. I worked the night shift at the Chapel Hill Police Department, would get off work at 7am and go straight to their classrooms to volunteer. Throughout this experience I discovered that kids, especially Black and brown kids, were being underserved. When I could do nothing more as a volunteer, I ran for School Board. During my time on the school board, I fought for better funding for our schools. I felt that the county was not adequately funding schools, so because I could do nothing more on the School Board, I ran for Orange County Commissioner. During my time as County Commissioner, I championed the construction of two schools, two senior centers, affordable housing initiatives, and more. Eventually, I reached a point where I could do nothing more as County Commissioner, so I ran for State House. Are you sensing a theme, Peter? | Friend,

I introduced the SAVE ACT - which will protect American voters and prevent illegal aliens from voting in federal elections.

But across the country -- illegal immigrants are being registered to vote. ONE CITIZEN. ONE VOTE.

That's the way it's been and that's what federal law requires.

The SAVE ACT would stop this and it should pass unanimously -- by both Republicans AND Democrats who believe in democracy and FAIR ELECTIONS.

In fact, the only reason to oppose this that I can think of is if you're comfortable with or want non-citizens to vote. Or want non-citizens to influence the outcome of our elections.

Friend, did you see Zoe’s last message? We want to make sure you saw her message regarding the second-to-last FEC deadline before the general election in November.

As our most critical deadline yet quickly approaches, it is more important than ever that we have a strong end-of-quarter report to publish for our opponents to see.

Friend,

One of our campaign’s most critical deadlines is quickly approaching. Sunday is the first public FEC fundraising deadline since Trump was convicted of 34 felonies and raised nearly $40 million from his MAGA supporters.

This means that our opponents are waiting for the moment our numbers go public. California is THE critical state in ensuring that we take back the House and every seat counts.

My top priority is protecting vulnerable California Democrats in this election, but I can’t do this without your help.

We are still $18,000 short of hitting our goal before this Sunday’s deadline, and we need to publish a strong report.

Can I count on you to rush a donation of $10 today to help me close our gap? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/zoe-june-24?amount=10]

Let’s show them that our grassroots base of supporters is strong enough to withstand their baseless attacks and misinformation campaigns.

I’m counting on you today, friend.

– Zoe

| Good afternoon,

What happened last night was important, important for the future of our nation. Many are concerned by what they saw on the debate stage and for different reasons. What I want to share with you today is what I think is very clear, Donald Trump continues to be dishonest in his representation of himself and his accomplishments. His repeated refusal to adhere to the basic tenets of our precious democracy are shocking and worrying. Unfortunately, my political opponent, Rick Allen, has never faltered in his support of the former president. I believe this is not the representation the citizens of Georgia’s 12th congressional district or the nation needs.

** A change is long overdue! **To make that change, we need to stay focused on the impact of what’s on the ballot, across the nation, in November.
## Every Woman’s Health and Reproductive Freedoms are on the ballot!

Being able to pay your rent or mortgage is on the ballot!

Being able to eat healthy and for many being able to even eat at all is on the ballot!

Higher Wages are on the ballot!

Being able to receive Emergency Medical Care and Preventive Health Care is on the ballot!

Social Security and Medicare are on the ballot!

Civil Rights, Voting Rights and Democracy are ALL on the ballot this November!
##
I am looking for people just like you to [join my team ](https://lizjohnsonforus.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d4a0fd0913238344008dfe952&id=7198104f39&e=e8eaba4639)and help me defeat Rick Allen in the upcoming election in November. If you are able, please also [make a donation of $25, $50 or $100 ](https://lizjohnsonforus.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d4a0fd0913238344008dfe952&id=704bb354a6&e=e8eaba4639)to help us do the important work necessary to reach every single voter with my message and plan for a brighter future. May I count on you? Thank you so much, Liz

| | | **PRESS RELEASE**

**Despite his anemic debate performance, Susie Lee continues to stand by Joe Biden’s side**
[_“For Democrats running down ballot, this is a serious problem_](https://DrewForNevada.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=faca3bfedb5031bc3491ebbc8&id=09892f8175&e=fc26432468)[ _.”_](https://DrewForNevada.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=faca3bfedb5031bc3491ebbc8&id=c18b2499e4&e=fc26432468)
June 28, 2024 Contact: [info@drewfornevada.com](mailto:press@drewfornevada.com)
(**Las Vegas, NV**) – [Despite President Joe Biden’s anemic debate performance](https://DrewForNevada.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=faca3bfedb5031bc3491ebbc8&id=f6a4878327&e=fc26432468), [record low approval ratings](https://DrewForNevada.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=faca3bfedb5031bc3491ebbc8&id=4200d7cf2e&e=fc26432468), and [polling numbers](https://DrewForNevada.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=faca3bfedb5031bc3491ebbc8&id=248e45c589&e=fc26432468) in Nevada that have members of the media and Democrat establishment calling for him to step aside, Susie Lee (NV-03) has made it exceedingly clear she stands with Biden every step of the way.

FiveThirtyEight shows that during the 117th Congress, despite touting herself as one of the most bipartisan members, [Susie Lee was nothing more than a puppet for the Biden administration, voting with Biden a perfect 100% of the time](https://DrewForNevada.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=faca3bfedb5031bc3491ebbc8&id=5f295e52e0&e=fc26432468).

“Susie Lee will continue to peddle the egregious lie that she is one of the most bipartisan members of Congress. This verifiable falsehood is a slap in the face to the voters of NV-03. She has been a rubber stamp for the Biden administration’s disastrous policies that are crippling hardworking Nevadans.

During Susie Lee’s tenure in Congress, in addition to being a unanimous supporter of the Biden agenda, the multimillionaire has made flippant comments about inflation, like, “ _Personally, I acknowledge things are getting more expensive, but I’m not going to apologize for it_ ,” [while inflation soars past 21% in Nevada](https://DrewForNevada.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=faca3bfedb5031bc3491ebbc8&id=e54754a21b&e=fc26432468).

Lee has criticized lawmakers for “ _obsessing over an ineffective and expensive border wall_ ,” despite over 75% of Nevada Latino voters being deeply concerned with the situation at the border and [estimates showing Las Vegas to be a top-15 city in the country for illegal immigrants.](https://DrewForNevada.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=faca3bfedb5031bc3491ebbc8&id=e181ea5382&e=fc26432468)

There's a reason why Nevada voters are so vehemently opposed to President Biden, his policies, and his lackeys like Susie Lee. Their glaring failures are destroying Southern Nevada’s working class, and I look forward to exposing her and President Biden's record to voters on the campaign trail.” **– Drew Johnson, Republican nominee in Nevada’s 3 rd congressional district**

Drew Johnson is running for one of America’s top targeted U.S. House seats. You can learn more about him and his candidacy by visiting DrewforNevada.com. _###_

subject: “A warmongering foreign lobbyist group bought Bowman’s seat”
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter, we’re still
reflecting on Tuesday’s deeply disappointing loss in New York’s 16th
congressional district.

It’s clear as day that Jamaal was targeted by AIPAC for his pro-peace,
pro-ceasefire stance. Jezebel’s Kylie Cheung correctly concluded:

“A warmongering foreign lobbyist group effectively bought Bowman’s seat,
all because he called for a ceasefire in Gaza and criticized the
atrocities perpetrated by Israel with our tax dollars.”

And Branko Marcetic of Jacobin pointed out:

“Bowman’s loss will soon be used — in fact, already is and was before the
polls even closed — by AIPAC and other pro-war forces to scare less
courageous candidates and members of Congress into line.”

But the truth is, while AIPAC takes its victory lap, its power is
weakening. This lobby group had to spend more in a primary race than it
ever had before — and more than has ever been spent on any single U.S.
House race — in order to win.

Even though AIPAC and other anti-Palestinian interests are trying to frame
Jamaal’s loss as a referendum on the pro-ceasefire movement, the reality
is that AIPAC barely mentioned Israel in their ads, because they know the
majority of voters support a ceasefire in Gaza and conditions on Israeli
military aid.

So it’s okay to feel sad, but we all need to draw inspiration from
Jamaal's unwavering commitment to justice both here and abroad. This
setback should not deter us from continuing our fight. We should feel
empowered that, despite the millions of dollars poured into this race,
people still showed up in amazing ways.

We witnessed incredible determination and mobilization from our Arab and
Muslim communities, the pro-Palestinian community, Black and Brown voters,
and everyday people who fought to make their communities better. So for
everyone who showed up for Jamaal by making contributions, phone banking,
knocking doors, and getting out the vote for our progressive champion:
your voices and efforts matter, in this and every election. This setback
highlights our power, and it is not the time to stop. We must continue our
fight and ensure we re-elect our next Squad member, Cori Bush. The stakes
couldn't be higher.

AIPAC and their right-wing donors think they can buy another race against
a pro-ceasefire incumbent in August: Rep. Cori Bush in Missouri’s 1st
district. They’ve already dumped $2 million into her opponent’s campaign,
and we know that’s just the beginning. But we won’t allow them to win.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20240628.CJ1D_q&refcode=em20240628-35516&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1001&akid=35516%2E1203867%2E-COwDN ]It’s up to us to come together as a progressive, grassroots movement
and stop them. Will you help us do it by pitching in $5
today?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20240628.CJ1D_q&refcode=em20240628-35516&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1020&akid=35516%2E1203867%2E-COwDN ]Contribute $5

Cori and the rest of our progressive Squad are standing with us, the
people, on the right side of history for justice and humanity. Now, for
the future of our Democratic Party, our country, and our world, we need to
stand with them.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

Last night, I spent 90 minutes debating on a stage with a guy who has all the morals of an alley cat. I mean, did you see Donald Trump last night? _He must have set a new record for the number of lies ever told in a single debate._ He lied about what a great economy he created, when we all remember the pandemic. He lied about how great he was for veterans, when we can recall how he called veterans who had given their lives for this country “suckers” and “losers.” **And he even lied about how he had nothing to do with January 6th.** **But we all saw it _with our own eyes_. _We saw the mob attack the Capitol. We saw the police being attacked. The Capitol ransacked._** Folks, for all of Trump’s lies last night, we did learn some important truths. _We learned he is still proud of being the person who killed Roe v. Wade.
We learned that he wants another giant tax cut for the very wealthy and biggest corporations.
And that he’ll cut your Medicare, your Social Security, and cut your health care to pay for it.
_Most dangerously -- though -- we learned again that Donald Trump will not respect the outcome of this year’s election.__ Donald Trump showed us who he is last night. We have to believe him. I mean, did you see Donald Trump last night? He must have set a new record for the number of lies ever told in a single debate. He lied about what a great economy he created, when we all remember the pandemic. He lied about how great he was for veterans, when we can recall how he called veterans who had given their lives for this country “suckers” and “losers.” And he even lied about how he had nothing to do with January 6th. But we all saw it with our own eyes. We saw the mob attack the Capitol. We saw the police being attacked. The Capitol ransacked. Folks, for all of Trump’s lies last night, we did learn some important truths. We learned he is still proud of being the person who killed Roe v. Wade. We learned that he wants another giant tax cut for the very wealthy and biggest corporations. And that he’ll cut your Medicare, your Social Security, and cut your health care to pay for it. Most dangerously -- though -- we learned again that Donald Trump will not respect the outcome of this year’s election. Donald Trump showed us who he is last night. #
---
Peter, Today marks 55 years since the Stonewall Uprising. On this day in 1969, police raided the Stonewall Inn, a haven for the LGBTQIA+ community that still stands in New York’s 10th Congressional District today as a beacon of the community. As police officers targeted LGBTQIA+ patrons, the brave individuals at Stonewall refused to back down. The groundbreaking Stonewall Uprising launched the LGBTQIA+ rights movement and inspired Pride Month itself. Today, Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, Rep. Ritchie Torres and I introduced resolutions in the Senate and House to name June 28 as Stonewall Day in commemoration of the Stonewall Uprising 55 years ago. But even as we celebrate how far we have come, Republican legislatures in states across the country are sowing division, launching regressive legislative attacks against the LGBTQIA+ community, and emboldening acts of hatred in our communities. Even just a couple of weeks ago, vandals destroyed a display of over 150 rainbow flags at the Stonewall National Monument. _During Pride Month. Peter._ **Let me be clear: Harassment like this has no place in NY-10, and I will always stand with the LGBTQIA+ community in the face of hate and discrimination.** I promise to always fight so that every New Yorker and every American can live with dignity, no matter how much bigotry or how many attacks Republicans level against the LGBTQIA+ community. body:
A NOTE FROM CHRISSY Summer brings some great opportunities to explore the many trails, preserves and parks in District 6! I hope you’ve been able to stay cool and spend some outside time with your families as I have. >From securing a big win for our local food bank to adding new faces to Team Chrissy, here's what I've been up to the last few weeks:

https://secure.actblue.com/contribute/page/houlahan-digital?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1000-ot-text

Protecting the House Intelligence Committee
I recently did something I thought I'd never have to do: Ask Speaker Johnson to remove and replace GOP Reps. Scott Perry and Ronny Jackson from the House Intel Committee. To put it plainly, these two men are unfit to serve in this critical role. I’m a veteran; I take our duty to those who serve seriously. We cannot allow someone who is under investigation for his role in the Jan. 6 attacks, or who is at risk of being compromised in any way by our adversaries, to serve on the very committee which oversees the intelligence community. This action has already made me a target of far-right extremists but I must be clear: the fight to preserve the integrity of our institutions and our national security is an important one, and I won’t back down.

https://secure.actblue.com/contribute/page/houlahan-digital?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1000-ot-text

Selective Service and the Draft
Selective Service and the draft are in the news a lot lately. Here’s why: Today, and since 1917, all men between the ages of 18-25 are required by law to register with the Selective Service. Not registering can result in a fine of up to $250,000 and up to five years in prison. Because registration numbers are dropping - due to the elimination of registration as part of the federal student loan process and the fact that fewer younger people are getting a driver’s license (where you also can register) - the federal government now spends $30 million each year to remind people to register. I believe there is an easier way that also saves taxpayer money, so I am supporting a resoundingly bipartisan plan to make registration automatic for men. I personally believe that this should also apply to women, but so far, that has not been passed. This is what’s being debated in Congress right now and why it’s in the news. I want to make it clear this is NOT a plan to reinstate the draft, and I hope we never again face a situation when that’s needed. Diplomacy and strength remains the best option for keeping our nation out of military entanglements.

https://secure.actblue.com/contribute/page/houlahan-digital?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1000-ot-text

Supporting the Fight Against Hunger in Our Community
Earlier this month, I had the opportunity to take a tour of the warehouse owned by Helping Harvest – the Feeding America member food bank serving our community members in Berks. This organization has been critical to the fight against hunger in our region. That's why I'm proud to share that I recently secured a $500,000 grant through the federal Community Project Funding Program that will support Helping Harvest as they construct their new community kitchen in downtown Reading. By supporting incredible organizations like theirs, I know we can build a better, healthier future for all of our neighbors.

https://secure.actblue.com/contribute/page/houlahan-digital?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1000-ot-text

Happy Pride!
This month, I am happy to celebrate Pride along with so many in our community! If you had the chance to be at Chester County Pride, then you know it was a great time. Berks Pride Fest is later this summer on July 21st. Hope to see you there! Now more than ever, shows of support like this are essential to building a world where our LGBTQ friends and family feel safe and welcome. Down in Washington, DC, I will keep fighting the far right's hateful attacks so our neighbors can openly be who they are and love who they love. Exciting Developments on Team Chrissy I'm so excited to report that we've recently onboarded our summer interns, which means that our field operations are ramping up! These dedicated young people are helping us to knock more doors, call more voters, and do more to engage the voters we need. You might even spot them in your neighborhood. Supporters like you make big developments like this possible, and together, we're building a team that can defeat the far right, protect our nation and our freedoms and elect Democrats up and down the ballot in November. That's all the news that's fit to print for June! I can't wait to share what I get up to in the months ahead as I fight for the needs of you and your family. In the meantime, happy Pride, and a very early happy Fourth!

There's work to be done,
Chrissy

It’s simple, friend: **T****he GOP knows that if they win in Nevada, they _will_ __ regain control of the White House and the Senate. **

# Trump Destroys Biden in Debate
### America First - Trump
| | | [Dan Carr](https://substack.com/@dancarr2014)
---
| Jun 28
---
| [](https://substack.com/@dancarr2014)
---
Dear Friend,
I wanted to share my thoughts on the debate that took place last night on CNN between Former President Donald Trump and President Joe Biden. It was clear that Trump delivered a commanding performance, highlighting his commitment to the America First agenda. I also will point out that the moderators did an excellent job in the way that they hosted the debate!!
Trump demonstrated his strong leadership skills and articulated a vision for the future that prioritizes American interests first. His points on the economy, national security, and many other topics showcased a deep understanding of the issues facing our nation and a clear plan to address them.
Biden struggled to present a coherent argument and seemed out of touch with the pressing needs of the American people. Trump's assertiveness and clarity made it evident that he is the obvious candidate to lead our country toward greater prosperity and security. In this debate there was only one man who was Presidential and that was Donald J. Trump!!!

My story is like so many immigrants in Arizona and our country today. My parents fled Fidel Castro’s communist Cuba in order to give me and my siblings a better life.

It was far from easy. Mom and Dad worked multiple jobs. My mother was even fired from a better-paying job for being pregnant with me.

But they persevered to give us a chance at the American Dream.

I am so grateful for their sacrifices. It moved me to have a career in broadcast journalism where I exposed corruption and held the powerful accountable.

I am so grateful for their sacrifices. It moved me to have a career in broadcast journalism where I exposed corruption and held the powerful accountable. Never did I think my story would culminate in me running for Congress. But circumstances led me to step up and fight back against the extremism we’re seeing today. I love our beautiful state of Arizona. I’ve lived here for over 36 years and raised my family here. I spent years working to build up our community.
